segments.t: The pretend engagement is going further than either of them expected. They talk about the registry office, and then both of them get cold feet. Listen first, and I'll explain afterwards.
Мы подадим заявление в загс?
Таня, у тебя есть знакомые в загсе?
Пожалуйста, помогите нам расписаться как можно быстрее.
Давайте расскажем эту новость всем гостям ресторана!
Подожди, кажется, я немножко поторопился.
Честно говоря, я тоже поторопилась с ответом.
Значит, нам обоим нужно хорошенько подумать.
Да, нам лучше немного подождать со свадьбой.
Шеф, вы поможете нам спокойно разобраться?
Шеф не хочет слушать наши семейные споры.
У Виктора сейчас начинается важный футбольный матч.
Тогда мы сами во всём разберёмся позже.
Иди работай, свадьба пока точно подождёт!
Let's unpack it.
Мы подадим заявление в загс?
загс

'Shall we apply at the registry office?' This is an old abbreviation for the civil registry office, and locals still say it. The phrase for applying translates to 'we will hand in an application'; the root action word is the same as the one used earlier for serving a dish.
Таня, у тебя есть знакомые в загсе?
знакомые

'Tanya, do you have acquaintances at the registry office?' This Listen to how 'acquaintances' comes from the phrase for getting to know someone. Listen to how 'you have' literally translates to 'at you there are'. Vika turns to her sister.
Пожалуйста, помогите нам расписаться как можно быстрее.
расписаться

'Please help us get married as fast as possible.' This word, literally 'sign each other', means to register a marriage. The speaker uses 'as fast as possible' translates to 'as fast as can be'. The sentence also includes the polite form for 'help'.
Давайте расскажем эту новость всем гостям ресторана!
Давайте
расскажем

'Let's tell this news to all the guests of the restaurant!' This gives 'let's tell', pairing the same root action word as the earlier complaint. The other phrase translates to 'to all the guests'. Vika raises the stakes.
Подожди, кажется, я немножко поторопился.
поторопился

'Wait, it seems I rushed a little.' This means 'I rushed', with a self-directed ending. We hear 'a little bit' is a softer version of the standard word. The sentence also includes We hear 'it seems'. Max starts to back away.
Честно говоря, я тоже поторопилась с ответом.
Честно
говоря

'To be honest, I also rushed with my answer.' This is a fixed phrase meaning 'honestly speaking'. The action When they say 'rushed' has the she-word ending. The last part means 'with the answer'. Vika backs away too.
Значит, нам обоим нужно хорошенько подумать.
нам
обоим
нужно

'So, both of us need to think carefully.' This literally translates to 'to us both it is needed'. Notice the part 'carefully' is a homely form of 'well', meaning 'properly'. The final action word means 'to think it over'.
Да, нам лучше немного подождать со свадьбой.
нам
лучше

'Yes, it is better for us to wait a little with the wedding.' For 'it is better for us', this translates to 'to us better'. In Russian, 'with the wedding' translates changes the ending of the thing word. The main action word means 'to wait a while'.
Шеф, вы поможете нам спокойно разобраться?
разобраться
'Chef, will you help us sort this out calmly?' This means 'to sort out', stemming from the earlier statement about the stove. The question uses the polite form of 'will you help'.
Шеф не хочет слушать наши семейные споры.
семейные
'The chef doesn't want to listen to our family arguments.' This is The way to express 'family' used as an descriptive word. The next word means 'arguments'. The chef has no time for them.
У Виктора сейчас начинается важный футбольный матч.
У

'Viktor has an important football match starting now.' This works like 'I have' is used here, literally meaning 'at Viktor' to express 'Viktor has', with the name taking a specific ending. The action 'is beginning' is used here takes a self-directed ending because the match begins on its own.
Тогда мы сами во всём разберёмся позже.
сами

'Then we will sort everything out ourselves later.' This Listen to how 'ourselves' puts the job back on the two of them. Listen to how 'we will sort everything out' literally means 'in everything we will sort ourselves out', using the same action word as before. The sentence ends with Listen to how 'later'.

'Go work, the wedding will definitely wait for now!' This is a combination of two commands, 'go' and 'work', with no conjunction. The speaker uses 'for now' is the same word used for 'bye'. The final action word means 'will wait'. Back to the full version.
